channels.name: CK
channels.purpose: Differential clock input (positive half). All command/address/control are sampled on the rising edge of CK at the CK/CK# crossing.
channels.active_levels: SSTL_15 differential; AC swing ≥ 0.350 V; Vix within ±150 mV of VDD/2
channels.idle_level: Continuously toggling during all states except Self-Refresh (after tCKSRE) and Reset

channels.name: CK#
channels.purpose: Differential clock input (negative half). Logical inverse of CK.

channels.name: CKE
channels.purpose: Clock Enable. HIGH activates internal clock and IO; LOW initiates Power-Down or Self-Refresh. Asynchronous for SR exit. Sampled with tIS/tIH on CK.
channels.active_levels: SSTL_15 single-ended; VIH_AC = VREF + 0.175 V; VIL_AC = VREF − 0.175 V

channels.name: CS#
channels.purpose: Chip Select / Rank Select. HIGH masks all commands; LOW asserts a command for one cycle. Part of every command code except DES.

channels.name: RAS#, CAS#, WE#
channels.purpose: Command inputs decoded together with CS# / CKE to encode MRS / REF / SRE / PRE / ACT / RD / WR / NOP / ZQ commands.

channels.name: BA[2:0]
channels.purpose: Bank Address. Selects 1 of 8 banks for ACT / RD / WR / PRE; selects 1 of 4 mode registers for MRS.

channels.name: A[15:0]
channels.purpose: Multiplexed address: row address during ACT; column address during RD/WR; op-code during MRS. A10/AP overloaded as auto-precharge; A12/BC# overloaded as on-the-fly burst chop.

channels.name: DM (DMU, DML for x16)
channels.purpose: Write Data Mask. HIGH coincident with DQ on a DQS edge masks the corresponding write byte. Pin shared with TDQS on x8.

channels.name: ODT
channels.purpose: On-Die Termination control. Enables RTT_Nom termination on DQ/DQS/DM in Synchronous / Dynamic / Asynchronous ODT modes. Ignored when MR1/MR2 RTT bits are zero and in Self-Refresh.

channels.name: RESET#
channels.purpose: Active-low asynchronous reset. CMOS rail-to-rail signal; LOW = reset asserted, HIGH = normal operation. DC HIGH = 80% of VDD; DC LOW = 20% of VDD.

channels.name: DQ[7:0] (x8)
channels.purpose: Data bus. Double data rate; sampled by receiver on both edges of DQS. DQ width = 4 / 8 / 16 per device organization.

channels.name: DQS, DQS# (DQSL/DQSU for x16)
channels.purpose: Bidirectional differential data strobe. Edge-aligned with DQ during read (DRAM driven); centred in DQ during write (controller driven). x4 has 1 pair, x8 has 1 pair, x16 has 2 pairs.

channels.name: TDQS, TDQS#
channels.purpose: Termination Data Strobe. Mirror of DQS termination resistance on the TDQS pin (which is the DM pin when TDQS disabled). x8 only.
channels.active_levels: Termination only — not a data strobe

channels.name: ZQ
channels.purpose: Reference pin for ZQ calibration. Connected to ground via 240 Ω ±1% external resistor.

channels.name: VREFDQ
channels.purpose: Reference voltage for DQ input thresholds. Nominal VDDQ/2.
channels.idle_level: Must remain stable in all states including Self-Refresh

channels.name: VREFCA
channels.purpose: Reference voltage for command/address input thresholds. Nominal VDD/2.
channels.idle_level: Must remain stable in all states including Self-Refresh

power_pins.name: VDD
power_pins.purpose: Power supply: 1.5 V ± 0.075 V (DDR3) / 1.35 V (DDR3L) / 1.25 V (DDR3U).

power_pins.name: VDDQ
power_pins.purpose: DQ Power Supply: same nominal as VDD; driven from the same regulator output.

channel_counts_quad_die_x8.note: Stacked / quad-die packages multiply CKE / CS / ODT / ZQ per die (CKE0/CKE1, CS0#..CS3#, ODT0/ODT1, ZQ0..ZQ3).

ordering_rules.data_byte_order_within_burst: Determined by MR0 A3 (RBT) and column-address bits A[2:0]; see Table 3 — Burst Type and Burst Order. BL8 sequential starting 000 → 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7; BL8 interleaved starting 001 → 1,0,3,2,5,4,7,6.

dependency_graph.common_rule: All commands are committed on the rising edge of CK. The DRAM is fully synchronous to CK except for asynchronous RESET# and asynchronous Self-Refresh exit on CKE.
dependency_graph.data_dependency: Read data on DQ depends on the prior RD command at deterministic latency RL = AL + CL. Write data acceptance depends on the prior WR command at deterministic latency WL = AL + CWL. There is no per-beat handshake.

handshake_pairs.name: CMD_DECODE
handshake_pairs.rule: Controller drives CKE / CS# / RAS# / CAS# / WE# / BA / A on the rising edge of CK; SDRAM decodes one command per cycle.

handshake_pairs.name: READ_BURST
handshake_pairs.rule: SDRAM drives 8 (BL8) or 4 (BC4) beats on DQ at RL = AL + CL from RD/RDA; DQS edge-aligned with DQ.

handshake_pairs.name: WRITE_BURST
handshake_pairs.rule: Controller drives 8 (BL8) or 4 (BC4) beats on DQ at WL = AL + CWL from WR/WRA; DQS centred in DQ.

handshake_pairs.name: ODT_SYNC
handshake_pairs.rule: ODT pin HIGH → RTT_Nom turns on after ODTLon = CWL + AL − 2; ODT LOW → RTT_Nom turns off after ODTLoff = CWL + AL − 2.

handshake_pairs.name: WRITE_LEVEL
handshake_pairs.rule: In WL mode (MR1 A7=1), DRAM samples CK on rising DQS edge and drives the sampled value back on DQ for the controller to read.

handshake_pairs.name: REFRESH
handshake_pairs.rule: Controller issues REF; SDRAM internally generates row addresses and refreshes all banks; tRFC must elapse before next command.

handshake_pairs.name: SELF_REFRESH_HANDOFF
handshake_pairs.rule: Controller drives CKE LOW with SRE; SDRAM holds itself in SR generating internal refreshes. Controller drives CKE HIGH with stable CK to exit; SDRAM completes pending refresh during tXS.
